one_line: This is a low-value, LPTA, year-round route contract for standard portable toilets at Zion. It is outside our fleet, price list, and NAICS/PSC codes, and it needs a local yard and pump truck to compete with the local incumbent, Wayne A. Levitz.
scope: NPS wants a contractor to rent, deliver, pump, clean, restock, repair or replace, and remove standard portable toilets at Zion National Park (Springdale, UT) from Jan 1, 2027 through Dec 31, 2031: a base year plus four one-year options. That is about 5–7 units across sites such as Nature Center, Big Bend, and Canyon Junction, serviced 1–3 times a week. Each unit must hold at least 60 gallons, have dual toilet paper dispensers and a wall-mounted waterless soap dispenser, and display our name. All waste is hauled off-site. Firm-fixed-price, NTE emergency CLINs (0011–0051) cover emergency placements, delivered within 24 hours of written notice, and emergency services, performed within 24 hours of a written Notice to Proceed.
fit: Set-aside fits our status: it is a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside (Sol. p.3; Amd 0002), with no 8(a), WOSB, SDVOSB, or HUBZone requirement. Our SAM is active, UEI REVFD44JLMV5, CAGE 57C31. Size under NAICS 562991 ($9M) still needs confirming.
Portable sanitation is one of our stated core competencies (Facility Support & Utilities: water delivery, waste removal, generators, portable sanitation).

Closest past performance: City and County of Denver SC-00011558 (restroom trailers with cleaning, pump-outs, waste disposal, supplies, maintenance) and USCG Station Lake Worth Inlet 70Z02826FMIAM0008 (restroom/shower trailers with wastewater support, $78,500).

Our operating model already covers weekly servicing, RCRA-compliant gray/black water removal, sanitizing, consumables, a 24/7 line, 24-hour on-site response for critical failures, and weekly QC reports.
No bonding, mandatory site visit, or specific license is stated in the solicitation. The certificate of insurance is due after award and is not an evaluation factor (Q&A #43).
red_flags: Off-core product: the SOW calls for standard portable toilets of at least 60 gallons. Our fleet and price list have restroom/shower trailers but no standard portable toilet item, and Technical Factor 2 requires a product, manufacturer, and part number.

Location: Zion is far from our Marina del Rey, CA base. The work is 1–3 services a week, year-round, with 24-hour repair or replacement, 24-hour emergency placement, no park dump station, and no water (Q&A #7, #28, #37). We would need a local yard and pump truck.
LPTA with quotes ranked lowest price first (Amd 0002). The local incumbent, Wayne A. Levitz (140P1222P0018), already has units in place, and the scope is 'generally the same' (Q&A #9, #38).

Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14, 50% for services) is now a checklist item. We would have to self-perform or use a similarly situated small-business sub, and a sub's markup would hurt us under LPTA.

Insurance must be carried by the prime, with the United States as named insured: $100K each person, $500K each occurrence, $500K property damage. The CO's view is that sub coverage does not satisfy it (Q&A #43).

The emergency figures (300 services/yr in FY27, 320 after; 15 placements in FY27, 30 after) are estimated quantities that count in the Total Evaluated Price at per-unit prices (Q&A #4, #35). The HigherGov summary misreads them as dollar prices.
The site visit (11/12/2026) has already passed. It was not stated as mandatory, and its time is inconsistent: 10AM MT in Amd 0002 versus 1PM in Q&A #8.
Funds are not currently available, and the solicitation may be cancelled (Subject to Availability of Funds addendum).
Service Contract Act applies, with two wage determinations attached (2015-5487 Washington County; 2015-5495 Beaver/Garfield/Iron/Kane). The revised SOW still reads 'ADD COUNTIES HERE'.

Errors in the solicitation documents: CLINs 0021–0051 all show a 2027 period of performance (Amd 0002). Several revised schedule tabs still say 'Temple* Septic Cleaning' even though septic was removed (Q&A #3, SOW §4). Amd 0001 said more SOW and pricing changes would follow.
Value is small: the estimate is $50,000–$180,000 over 5 years. Our past performance is restroom trailers, not standard portable toilet route service.
competition: Incumbent: Wayne A. Levitz, Contract 140P1222P0018. It owns and services the units now on site, and the new scope is 'generally the same' (Q&A #9, #38). Similar DOI awards under NAICS 562991 drew 1–13 offers. Examples: A & G Pumping, PINN portable toilets, 13 offers. EL Dorado Septic, 5 offers. Short Septic, 5. Kevin's Pro Clean, 5. River Septic, 3. D&M Pumping, 2. All winners are regional pumping and sanitation firms. None of the listed past awards was in Utah, and the incumbent's award value is not given.
price_signal: HigherGov puts the estimated value at $50,000–$180,000 total for 5 years. Comparable awards: A & G Pumping, PINN Portable Toilet Rental & Servicing, $51,350 (about 1 year, 13 offers). Brown & Jackson, Yakima Canyon porta potty rental, $11,270 (2 years). D&M Pumping, portable and vault toilet services, $277,330 (5 years). EL Dorado Septic, restroom pumping and portable rentals, $380,677 (3 years). Suntiff, portable toilets, $407,352 (2 years). Our price list has no standard portable toilet line. The nearest item, a 13ft Luxury Shower-Restroom Combination Trailer, is priced at 2,995–3,995 with no stated billing basis, so we cannot price this job from our list.

Technical Factor 1, Draft Schedule, with delivery starting 1 Jan 2027 and milestones for the base and option periods (Award Selection Process).

Technical Factor 2, Product Data: portable toilet product, manufacturer, and part number (if available), meeting the 60-gallon minimum, dual toilet paper dispensers, wall-mounted waterless soap, and supplier name on each unit (Award Selection Process; Revised SOW §3–4).
Technical Factor 3, Operations Plan: adding toilets with notice, prep, and delivery times; relocation; maintenance frequency; and replacement timing (Award Selection Process).
Limitations on Subcontracting worksheet (Attachment 5) or an equivalent showing compliance with the 50% limit (Amd 0002 checklist; FAR 52.219-14).
Active SAM registration, UEI, and small business size under NAICS 562991 ($9M) at quote, award, and throughout performance (Sol. Section I; Q&A #6).

Post-award: DOI 1452.228-70 insurance certificate naming the US ($100K/person, $500K/occurrence, $500K property damage); Safety Plan and Spill Plan; quarterly usage reports; IPP invoicing (Sol. clauses; Revised SOW §3).

Performance: graffiti removed within 24 hours; damaged units repaired or replaced within 24 hours; emergency placement within 24 hours of written notice; emergency service within 24 hours of a written Notice to Proceed; serious incidents reported within 3 hours; SCA wage determination compliance; no ATVs (Revised SOW §3, §5, §9; Sol. clauses).
